title: fix: cuda-graph shape guard warmup regression
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Fixes a warmup regression in CUDA graph capture/replay when using shape guards; no user-facing API changes.
description:
Background: Recent changes added CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and an aggressive warmup path intended to reduce first-request latency. After rolling this out we observed a regression on variable-length workloads where warmup could incorrectly prime the runtime with the wrong shape-guarded graph, leading to degraded startup latency and KV-cache priming failures under certain scheduling paths.

This PR: - Fixes the warmup regression by ensuring shape-guard keys are canonicalized during capture and replay. The capture logic now records the exact shape-guard fingerprint together with stream affinity, and replay is gated by an exact-match check to avoid replaying a graph captured for a different guard. - Adjusts the warmup path so that KV cache priming is run in a deterministic order before any graph replay. This prevents missed KV priming when a replay path takes a fast path that previously skipped priming. - Adds a guard in the scheduler to avoid triggering concurrent captures for the same logical shape while a capture is in-flight. This removes a race that could cause duplicate warmups and an apparent performance regression. - Adds e2e perf tests and unit coverage around shape-guard matching, plus a CI perf step that verifies startup p50/p95 against a golden baseline.

Testing and validation: Local microbenchmarks and CI perf job were run with a mixture of sequence-length distributions (8/64/2048). Before the fix we saw median startup (first-token) increase from ~22ms to ~45ms for mixed workloads; after this change the p50 returns to ~21ms and p95 is improved compared to the regression. We also validated boolean correctness of KV cache hits across multiple replay scenarios.

Motivation: This regression impacted some Dedicated customers running mixed-sequence workloads and was surfaced by an internal performance alert (ENG-4823). The change is conservative: it does not change public APIs or model artifacts, only the runtime capture/replay and warmup sequencing logic.
